record.paper_title: Open problems and some results on strongly closed subalgebras of B(X)
record.context_brief: Containment in maximal strongly closed algebras
record.original_question: Let X be a Banach space and let B(X) be the algebra of bounded linear operators on X. For a closed subspace M of X^n in general position, define A(M) to be the set of operators T in B(X) such that (x_1,...,x_n) in M implies (T x_1,...,T x_n) in M. A proper strongly closed subalgebra A of B(X) is of order n if A is contained in some such A(M) over X^n and is not contained in any such construction over X^k for k<n; an m.s.c.a. is a maximal strongly closed algebra. If A is any proper strongly closed subalgebra of B(X), must A be contained in some m.s.c.a., and more specifically in some m.s.c.a. of the same order as A?

evidence.quote: Problem 1. Let A be a proper strongly closed subalgebra of B(X) , is it contained in some m.s.c.a. (or in some m.s.c.a. of the same order) ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a Banach space and let $B(X)$ denote the algebra of all bounded linear operators on $X$, equipped with the strong operator topology. For a positive integer $n$, a closed subspace $M \subseteq X^n$ is said to be in general position if its projection onto each coordinate factor is dense (and $M$ is not reducible to a subspace of $X^k$ with $k<n$ in any coordinate-permutation sense). To each such $M$ associate the subalgebra
$$A(M) = \{\, T \in B(X) : (x_1,\dots,x_n) \in M \ \Rightarrow \ (Tx_1,\dots,Tx_n) \in M \,\}.$$
Each $A(M)$ is a strongly closed unital subalgebra of $B(X)$. A proper strongly closed subalgebra $A \subseteq B(X)$ is said to be of order $n$ if $A \subseteq A(M)$ for some closed subspace $M \subseteq X^n$ in general position, but $A$ is not contained in any $A(N)$ with $N \subseteq X^k$ in general position for any $k<n$. A maximal strongly closed algebra (m.s.c.a.) is a proper strongly closed subalgebra of $B(X)$ that is maximal among such subalgebras with respect to inclusion.

Prove or disprove: every proper strongly closed subalgebra $A$ of $B(X)$ is contained in some m.s.c.a.; moreover, $A$ is contained in some m.s.c.a. of the same order as $A$.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return any source explicitly resolving the question of whether every proper strongly closed subalgebra of $B(X)$ is contained in a maximal strongly closed subalgebra (or in one of the same order). General references on strong operator topology and von Neumann algebras do not address this specific Banach-space-level problem, so its status remains unverified.
